newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton closes up ahead of USDA export report.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton closes up ahead of USDA export report.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures settled sharply higher on mixed buying amid bullish sentiment for Friday's weekly export and sales report, market sources said.
They expect sales to total about 150,000 bales. The U.S. Department of Agriculture will release its report at 0830 EST Friday. The data are normally issued Thursday.

The most-active May contract pierced its nearby resistance target early and continued to accumulate gains, lifted initially by trade buying. The buying pushed May into stops around 74.50 cents and above, prompting the speculators to become aggressive buyers later in the session.
May closed 1.33 higher at 75.18 cents per pound, traded 75.30 to 73.90 cents. Spot-March ended up 1.10 to 73.33 cents.
Open interest in May rose 3,778 lots to 33,962 lots.
Volume was estimate at 20,000 lots compared with Wednesday's official volume of 24,584 lots.
Heavy rains in Australia and South America could damage quality and yields in those crops and eventually boost U.S. exports, now pegged at 6.5 million bales for the current crop year.
"That could hold the key for U.S. exports," O.A. Cleveland, a cotton marketing specialist with Mississippi State Universtiy, said.
Cleveland noted that the December contract, which growers monitor to gauge planted agreage, has remained around 76.00 cents even as the old crop hit fresh contract lows earlier in the week.
"That says to me that the market is recognizing that we have to keep it at 76.00 cents and up to entice the cotton acreage we need," he said.
